title: X-ray fluorescence microscopy scanning of Drosophila oocytes and eggs
protocol: Isolate the desired samples from flies.
Prepare isolated samples for mounting.
Perform sample isolation and mounting on the same day.
Isolate Drosophila oocytes following the protocol for mounting and scanning.
Dissect ovaries to collect oocytes at desired stages using morphology identification.
Trigger Drosophila egg activation during ovulation in vivo.
Activate Drosophila oocytes in vitro by applying mechanical pressure or swelling.
Incubate mature stage-14 oocytes in hypotonic solutions for in vitro activation.
Dissect 3- to 5-day-old virgin females and isolate oocytes of desired stages in isolation buffer (IB).
Release oocytes by teasing apart dissected ovaries on a microscope slide using forceps.
Isolate oocytes based on morphology for further processing.
Collect laid eggs over a short time-window (30 or 60 min) to obtain embryos at a desired stage.
Age collected eggs for a controlled period of time.
Verify stages of embryos by DAPI-staining a subset of the collected eggs.
Dechorionate embryos manually if necessary, to allow desiccation.
Mate virgin females overnight (14–16 h) with spermless males.
Transfer female flies to a grape juice agar plate on the second day.
Allow females to lay eggs for ∼5 hours at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Collect laid eggs by washing them off the plate with egg wash buffer.
Wash each egg or oocyte twice in mounting buffer (MB).
Rinse immature oocytes up and down in MB using a glass Pasteur pipette.
Handle immature oocytes gently to avoid mechanical activation or damage.
Accumulate samples in MB and mount them on SiN windows on the day of collection.
Place a 5 mm × 5 mm SiN window glued to an aluminum stick with clear nail polish on the stage of a dissecting microscope.
Add a 1 μL drop of MB in the middle of the SiN window carefully.
Avoid contacting the SiN window with the pipette tip to prevent breaking it.
Gently transfer an oocyte or egg to the liquid drop with forceps.
Grab the oocyte or egg by the dorsal appendages for ease of manipulation and to avoid pressure on the oocyte body.
Take extra care not to contact the window with the forceps.
Mount three or four oocytes or eggs on the same window.
Blot off extra mounting buffer (MB) with a Kimwipe touched to the edge of the drop.
For immature oocytes without dorsal appendages, mount by pipetting approximately 5 μL MB containing the oocytes onto the middle of the window and blotting off the excess MB as described.
Prepare 3 to 4 windows for each stage examined for a total of 10 to 15 oocytes.
Air-dry the windows by placing them in a closed petri dish at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 30 minutes.
Store windows with samples on them in a closed petri dish.
Place the petri dish in a sealed secondary container with desiccant until XFM scanning.
Apply for beamtime in advance at Argonne National Laboratories or a similar facility that offers XFM scanning.
Scan mounted specimens using XFM.
Rotate sample 15 degrees toward the detector during XRF detection.
Perform horizontal scans either in fly mode or step mode, depending on the specific equipment settings.
Conduct vertical scans exclusively in step mode as required by the Argonne XFM setup.
Mount specimens on SiN windows onto aluminum sticks.
Place three windows per stick in kinematic mounts for Microprobe setup.
Fit the samples into chambers filled with He to reduce air scatter, decay of X-ray emitted by samples, and signals from Ar.
Set the X-ray beam to 10.3 KeV using a 3.3 cm undulator and Si 111 monochromator.
Trim the beam using a 500 μm pinhole.
Focus the beam with a Fresnel zone plate (320 μm /100 nm).
Select the first order using a 30 μm order-sorting aperture.
Tilt the sample towards the detector by 15°.
Scan the sample through the X-ray beam using translation stages with Epics controls.
Collect X-ray fluorescence spectra using Vortex ME 4 and xMap DXP readout system.
Measure X-ray absorption by the sample using two ion chambers for normalization.
